pr_comments: @starkillerOG when referencing an issue that you want the PR to fix, note that you either need to use a link or a `#` letter and then the issue number. You can't put a `#` in front of the link.

> Please improve the error message to have the username and and auth level injected as placeholders instead of a message in English.

@joncar, @emontnemery I have tried injecting the username and user_level directly in the error message like this:
```
errors[CONF_USERNAME] = "not_admin"  
placeholders["username"] = host.api.username
 placeholders["user_level"] = host.api.user_level

  return self.async_show_form(
      step_id="user",
      data_schema=data_schema,
      errors=errors,
      description_placeholders=placeholders,
  )
```

with the strings/en translation:
`"not_admin": "User needs to be admin, {username} has authorisation level {user_level}",`

But when I tested this on my dev enviroment it displayed the error message without replacing `{username}` and `{user_level}`
But just displayed:
`User needs to be admin, {username} has authorisation level {user_level}`

When putting it in the description (like done now) it did work and `{username}` and `{user_level}` were replaced by "TestUser" and "guest".

What am I doing wrong?
Run the translations script in `develop` mode for the integration and make sure you reload the browser page once after starting Home Assistant.
@MartinHjelmare thanks for the help, I have fixed the issue.

@MartinHjelmare I implemented the reauth flow as you requested.
Could you have a look and review/merge?
@emontnemery The error message now has the username and auth level injected as placeholders instead of a hard coded message in English. Could you approve this PR?
@MartinHjelmare thanks for the review, I have processed all feedback

issue_context.title: Reolink integration ONVIF errors with NVR RLN8-410
issue_context.body:
### The problem

It looks like there are some compatibility issues with the latest Reolink firmware. It doesn't appear to cause any issues, but the log is listing these errors at Reolink integration startup:

``` 
2023-01-08 18:43:52.947 ERROR (MainThread) [reolink_aio.api] Host 192.168.1.80:443: connection error: Cannot connect to host 192.168.1.80:8000 ssl:default [Connect call failed ('192.168.1.80', 8000)].
2023-01-08 18:43:53.647 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.reolink.host] ONVIF is disabled on NVR, trying to enable it
2023-01-08 18:43:53.647 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.reolink.host] RTSP is disabled on NVR, trying to enable it
2023-01-08 18:43:53.687 ERROR (MainThread) [reolink_aio.api] Host 192.168.1.80:443: command "SetNetPort" error.
2023-01-08 18:43:53.689 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.reolink.host] Failed to enable ONVIF on NVR. Set it to ON to receive notifications
2023-01-08 18:43:53.691 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.reolink.host] Failed to enable RTSP on NVR. Set it to ON
2023-01-08 18:43:54.510 ERROR (MainThread) [reolink_aio.api] Host 192.168.1.80:443: command GetPowerLed response channel 0 does not equal requested channel 1
2023-01-08 18:43:54.512 ERROR (MainThread) [reolink_aio.api] Host 192.168.1.80:443: command GetPowerLed response channel 0 does not equal requested channel 2
2023-01-08 18:43:54.514 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.reolink] Finished fetching reolink.NVR data in 0.822 seconds (success: True)
2023-01-08 18:43:54.515 INFO (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.camera] Setting up camera.reolink
2023-01-08 18:43:54.901 ERROR (MainThread) [reolink_aio.api] Host 192.168.1.80:443: command GetPowerLed response channel 0 does not equal requested channel 1
2023-01-08 18:43:54.904 ERROR (MainThread) [reolink_aio.api] Host 192.168.1.80:443: command GetPowerLed response channel 0 does not equal requested channel 2
2023-01-08 18:43:54.905 DEBUG (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.reolink] Finished fetching reolink.NVR data in 0.387 seconds (success: True)
```

Firstly, it looks like ONVIF is broken on the latest Reolink firmware for my NVR. It's supposedly "on", but port 8000 isn't accepting any connections. It would be nice if we could disable ONVIF features in the Reolink addon.

Secondly, the integration tries and fails to turn on ONVIF/RTMP and RTSP at startup (whether they are on or off already), which adds errors to the log.

I also get a lot of repeated logs like this during operation:
```
2023-01-08 18:35:35.726 ERROR (MainThread) [reolink_aio.api] Host 192.168.1.80:443: command GetPowerLed response channel 0 does not equal requested channel 1
```
Which looks like a bug in the library.

With my NVR, some of these API calls apparently fail.
* Model: RLN8-410
* Build No.: 22120247
* Hardware: No. N2MB02
* Firmware Version: v3.2.0.214_22120247

Manually enabling RTMP and ONVIF doesn't help avoid the error.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.1.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

N/A

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Reolink

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/reolink

### Diagnostics information

[home-assistant_reolink_2023-01-08T18-44-00.072Z.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/10369228/home-assistant_reolink_2023-01-08T18-44-00.072Z.log)


### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

I'm happy to provide additional diagnosis if needed!

@MarkGodwin thanks for reporting the errors.
The `command GetPowerLed response channel 0 does not equal requested channel 1` has already been fixed in the upstream library and schould be part of the next patch release of HomeAssistant.

The cannot connect to port 8000 error is because the ONVIF port is not open in your NVR.
This port can only be opend from the NVR itself using a mouse and screen (not the mobile app, web app or windows client).
It is also possible to open the port using the API which the integration is trying.
I have tested this and it works on my RLN8-410 with firmware v3.2.0.214_22120252, hardware N3MB01

Are you using a admin account in the reolink HomeAssistant integration?
Ah, good point, I am not using an admin account. That would explain it.

@MarkGodwin please try it out with a admin account and report back if the errors disapear.
If that solves it, I will make a note in the HomeAssistant documentation that a admin account is needed, and also add to the error message in the log that a admin acount is required.

Ok, using an admin account has fixed the warnings about ONVIF/RTMP/RTSP.

When I deleted and re-created the addin (the only way I could change the account details), I got this:
``` 
2023-01-08 20:11:44.772 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.reolink.config_flow] Unexpected exception
Traceback (most recent call last):
File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/reolink/config_flow.py", line 73, in async_step_user
host = await async_obtain_host_settings(self.hass, user_input)
File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/reolink/config_flow.py", line 129, in async_obtain_host_settings
if not await host.async_init():
File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/reolink/host.py", line 93, in async_init
if not await self._api.set_net_port(
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/reolink_aio/api.py", line 1688, in set_net_port
response = await self.send_setting(body)
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/reolink_aio/api.py", line 2616, in send_setting
await self.get_state(cmd=getcmd)
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/reolink_aio/api.py", line 782, in get_state
body.extend(ch_body)
UnboundLocalError: local variable 'ch_body' referenced before assignment
```
But it worked ok on the second attempt, after selecting the "Use Https" checkbox.

Port 8000 is now open, too. I rebooted the NVR so it may have been that. Glad I didn't have to attach a screen and mouse - the NVR is hard to get to.

@MarkGodwin thank you for your feedback.
PR https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/25662 adds a note in the documentation that a admin account is needed.
PR https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/85570 will force the use of a admin account by checking the admin privilages during init and config flow so this can never happen again.
PR https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/85571 bumps the upstream library to fix the "UnboundLocalError: local variable 'ch_body' referenced before assignment" error.

If you appreciate the reolink integration and want to support its development, please consider [sponsering](https://github.com/sponsors/starkillerOG) the upstream library.
